- Conditioning finisher (Phase 2–3 optional): short low‑impact circuits or intervals (e.g., 4 x 2 min easy cycling with 2 min easy recovery) keeping HR below limit.
- Cool down and stretching: 8–10 minutes low HR activity and static stretches; breathing exercises.

Detailed week‑by‑week program

Phase 1 — Weeks 1–4: Foundation
Goals: establish routine, teach breathing, build aerobic base, introduce resistance, focus on symmetry and balance.

Weeks 1–2 (3x resistance days + 2x light aerobic)
Resistance sessions (Mon/Wed/Fri): Use machines or cable-based movements to control load. Monitor HR and RPE.

Session structure:
- Warm‑up: 8–10 min treadmill walk or recumbent cycle at easy pace (HR well below 115).
- Resistance circuit (perform 2 rounds in Week 1; 2–3 rounds Week 2). 60–90 s rest between sets/exercises as needed.
  1. Seated chest press (machine) — 2 sets × 12–15 reps
  2. Seated row (machine/cable) — 2 × 12–15
  3. Leg press (or seated step) — 2 × 12–15 (avoid Valsalva; breathe)
  4. Seated overhead press with light dumbbells (or machine) — 2 × 10–12
  5. Seated or supported single‑leg stands / assisted step‑ups — 2 × 10 each leg (or 30 s hold)
  6. Bodyweight or assisted squats to chair — 2 × 12–15
  7. Modified plank (knees) or pallof press (core) — 2 × 20–30 s
- Cool‑down: 8 min slow walking/cycling, then gentle stretching (chest, hamstrings, quads, calves, hip flexors) and diaphragmatic breathing practice (5 breaths sets).

Light aerobic sessions (Tue/Thu):
- 20–30 min steady state low‑impact (treadmill walk, recumbent bike, elliptical) at easy–moderate intensity (RPE 10–12). Include 5 min warm‑up and 3–5 min cool down. Add 5–10 min balance/mobility: tandem stand, single leg balance with support (15–30 s), ankle mobility.

Weeks 3–4
Progressions:
- Increase resistance sets to 3 where tolerated and increase reps to 10–15 depending on load. Slightly increase aerobic duration to 30–35 min on aerobic days if HR and symptoms are fine.
- Resistance session: progress to 3 rounds of the circuit (or 3 sets per exercise), keeping rest 60–90 s. Add or swap exercises:
  - Replace seated chest press with light dumbbell bench on incline (supported) if technique is good.
  - Add lat pulldown instead of row occasionally.
  - Add calf raises (standing with support) 3 × 12–15.
  - Add seated hip abduction/adduction machine 2–3 × 12.
- Introduce low‑impact interval work at end of one resistance day: 4 × 1 minute slightly higher cadence cycling with 2 minutes easy recovery, monitor HR closely and keep below limit.

Phase 2 — Weeks 5–8: Build
Goals: increase aerobic duration and endurance, increase resistance volume slightly, add more functional movements and light circuit training.

Weekly plan remains 3 resistance + 2 aerobic/moderate activity days.

Weeks 5–6
Resistance sessions (Mon/Wed/Fri):
- Warm‑up: 10 min walking/elliptical with mobility
- Resistance program: 3 sets each exercise, 10–14 reps, 60–75 s rest. Slightly increase load but keep RPE 11–13.
  1. Incline machine chest press or light dumbbell incline press — 3 × 10–12
  2. Seated cable/hammer row or supported single‑arm row — 3 × 10–12
  3. Goblet squat to bench (light kettlebell/dumbbell) — 3 × 10–12 (or leg press 3 × 10–12)
  4. Cable or machine shoulder press (seated) — 3 × 10–12
  5. Romanian deadlift with light dumbbells/toes slightly bent — 3 × 10–12 (focus on hip hinge)
  6. Step‑ups (low step) alternating — 3 × 10 each leg
  7. Standing anti‑rotation press (Pallof) or cable woodchop — 3 × 10 each side
  8. Balance exercise: single‑leg RDL support or standing hip hinge with support — 2 × 10 each leg
- Conditioning finisher (optional, once/week): 6–8 minutes easy circuit — e.g., 30 s row (light) + 60 s marching in place × 4, keep HR monitored.

Light aerobic days (Tue/Thu):
- 30–40 minutes steady state brisk walking or elliptical at moderate intensity (RPE 11–13), keep HR <115. Add progressive walking hills on treadmill with low grade but maintain HR limit (short 30–60 s incline bouts). Finish with 10 min flexibility and breathing.

Weeks 7–8
Progression:
- Slightly increase time of aerobic sessions to 35–45 min as tolerated.
- Resistance sessions: maintain 3 sets but add one more functional movement or light unilateral exercise, and introduce tempo control (3 s eccentric). Continue to avoid heavy loads; keep RPE 11–13.
  Example alterations:
  - Replace goblet squat occasionally with box squat or split squat (assisted).
  - Add seated cable anti‑shear core work and farmer carry with very light dumbbells (20–40 m) focusing on posture and breathing.
- Conditioning finisher: 3 rounds of low‑impact circuit (45 s work / 60 s easy): stationary bike easy, step‑ups, band rows. Keep HR controlled.

Phase 3 — Weeks 9–12: Consolidate and maintain
Goals: increase functional capacity, maintain cardiac limits, slightly increase complexity and dual task balance, prepare for long‑term independence.

Weeks 9–10
Resistance days:
- Warm‑up: 10 min aerobic + mobility
- Resistance circuit: 3 sets × 8–12 reps for main lifts; introduce controlled superset pairs for efficiency but keep rest and HR monitored.
  1. Dumbbell/controlled machine bench press or incline press — 3 × 8–12
  2. Single‑arm cable row or TRX row — 3 × 8–12
  3. Bulgarian split squat (assisted) or step‑downs — 3 × 8–10 each leg
  4. Romanian deadlift or light trap bar deadlift (low load) — 3 × 8–10
  5. Seated overhead press alternating with lateral raises (lighter) — 3 × 8–12
  6. Core: dead bug variations / Pallof press — 3 × 10–12
  7. Balance and proprioception: single‑leg stands progressing to eyes closed or foam pad 2 × 30 s
- Conditioning: 10 min steady bike/elliptical at moderate intensity or interval: 5 × 2 minutes slightly higher cadence with 2 minutes easy between.

Light aerobic days:
- 40–50 min brisk walking or elliptical, can include longer gentle inclines/walking outdoors. Continue balance and flexibility.

Weeks 11–12
Final progression and consolidation:
- Continue 3 resistance days, maintain 3 sets; you may increase slightly to 3–4 sets on tolerated exercises (avoid pushing beyond RPE 13).
- Add more functional multi‑joint activities: farmers carry (light), suitcase carries, timed sit‑to‑stands, repeated step ups (low height).
- Conditioning: one session per week can include longer continuous aerobic work (50–60 min) at moderate intensity if tolerated and HR remains below limit. Other cardio sessions remain 30–40 min.
- Introduce more dual‑task balance (marching while tossing light ball) to improve daily function.

Sample week (Week 12) session example (Mon):
- Warm‑up 10 min treadmill walk
- Circuit (3 rounds):
  - Incline DB press 3 × 10
  - TRX row 3 × 10
  - Assisted Bulgarian split squat 3 × 8 each
  - RDL with light DB 3 × 10
  - Pallof press 3 × 12
  - Farmer carry 3 × 30 m (very light)
- 10 min easy bike cool down + stretching + diaphragmatic breathing.

Precautions, monitoring and modifications
- Teach proper breathing: exhale on exertion, inhale on recovery. Cue to avoid Valsalva on every exercise.
- Use interval adjustments: if HR approaches 115 bpm, stop exercise, rest until HR decreases and then continue at lower intensity. Prefer longer rest intervals, fewer sets, or lower resistance.
- Use machines and supported movements early; progress to free weights only when technique and stability are solid.
- If on beta‑blockers, HR will be blunted — use RPE as primary intensity gauge (aim for RPE 11–13). Adjust HR targets if medication affects readings.
- Watch for signs of intolerance: chest pain, undue dyspnea (beyond RPE), dizziness, palpitations, undue fatigue. Stop and follow emergency plan if chest pain or concerning signs.
- Avoid isometric and maximal contractions (no 1RM testing). No breath‑holding.

Nutrition & recovery guidance (cardiac focus)
- Aim for heart‑healthy eating: Mediterranean‑style pattern — emphasis on vegetables, fruits, whole grains, legumes, nuts, olive oil, lean protein (fish, poultry), limit saturated fat, trans fats, processed meats, excess sodium, and added sugars.
- Sodium: aim for <2,300 mg/day (or individualized per cardiologist). If heart failure or other conditions require stricter limits, follow clinician guidance.
- Protein: moderate intake to support muscle maintenance — ~1.0–1.2 g/kg/day (adapt per renal function). Spread across meals.
- Hydration: regular hydration before/during/after workouts; avoid overhydration but ensure sensible fluid intake.
- Meal timing: avoid heavy meals immediately before exercise; small snack 1–2 hours before if needed.
- Weight management: aim for gradual weight loss if needed (0.25–0.5 kg/week) via moderate caloric deficit and physical activity. Emphasize long‑term sustainable changes.
- Alcohol: follow clinician advice; generally moderate to low recommended.
- Supplementation: prioritize whole foods; discuss omega‑3s, vitamin D, or others with physician if appropriate.

Recovery & other considerations
- Sleep: aim for 7–9 hours/night.
- Flexibility and mobility: 10–15 minutes after workouts for major muscle groups; include breathing practice and relaxation.
- Stress management: include relaxation techniques (diaphragmatic breathing, progressive muscle relaxation, or brief guided meditation) to support autonomic balance.
- Follow‑up: recheck with cardiology/cardiac rehab as scheduled and consider a structured graded exercise test/functional assessment before substantially increasing intensity.
- Reassess progress every 4 weeks: review BP, HR responses, RPE, functional improvements, balance and gait, and adjust program accordingly.

Outcome measures to track
- Resting HR and BP trends
- Submaximal exercise HR response for set activities (e.g., 6‑minute walk or 10‑minute treadmill at set speed)
- RPE for typical sessions
- Functional tests: sit‑to‑stand count (30 s), timed up and go (TUG), single‑leg balance time
- Strength: number of repetitions at chosen load or progression in load if RPE remains controlled

- Adequate protein for muscle maintenance during training — roughly 1.0–1.2 g/kg bodyweight/day unless medical conditions require otherwise.
- Alcohol in moderation (if permitted) — no more than 1 standard drink/day and check with physician.
- Avoid crash diets; aim for gradual, sustainable weight loss if needed (≈0.25–0.5 kg/week) via a modest calorie deficit.

Estimated energy and macronutrient framework

- Protein: 1.0–1.2 g/kg/day (e.g., 70–100 g/day for a 70–85 kg man).

Daily structure and meal examples
Aim for 3 balanced meals + 1–2 small snacks as needed to support training and energy. Time meals around workouts: light carbohydrate + protein 1–2 hours before sessions if needed; a balanced recovery snack/meal within 60–90 minutes after training (carb + protein).

Sample day (approx. 2,000 kcal) — swap portions to adjust calories
- Breakfast:

- Mid‑morning snack (optional):
  - 1 small apple + 12–15 raw almonds.

Heart‑healthy food swaps and guidance
- Fats: Use extra virgin olive oil instead of butter. Snack on nuts/seeds instead of chips. Limit processed baked goods and margarine high in trans fats.

- Aim for slow, steady weight loss (if needed) — 0.25–0.5 kg/week — by combining modest caloric reduction and regular physical activity. Larger deficits are not advised after recent MI without clinician oversight.

- Small sustainable changes: swap processed snacks for nuts/fruit; cook oily fish twice weekly; use olive oil; increase vegetables to 4–6 cups/day.

That said, you can increase caloric expenditure and accelerate weight loss while staying within the moderate‑intensity prescription by safely increasing duration, frequency, and density of cardio and by making adjustments to resistance training and nutrition. Safe strategies to increase energy expenditure without exceeding HR limits
1. Increase total cardio duration and frequency
- Add extra low–moderate sessions: move from 2 light aerobic days to 3–4, and increase session length (e.g., 30 → 45–60 minutes), keeping HR below ~115 bpm.
- Split sessions: two shorter sessions per day (e.g., 25–30 min morning + 20–30 min afternoon) can raise total expenditure and often keeps peak HR lower than a single longer bout.

Detailed guidance

1) Don’t add HIIT until he’s medically cleared
- Before introducing true high‑intensity interval training (HIIT) that will raise HR above his current limit (~70% age‑predicted max ≈ ~115 bpm), obtain written clearance from his cardiologist or cardiac rehab team. Useful items to request from the clinician:
  - Explicit permission to progress above 70% age‑predicted max (state target HR or approval for %VO2peak).
  - Recent exercise stress test or cardiopulmonary exercise test (CPET) demonstrating safe responses at higher workloads and a safe peak HR/workload.
  - Any medication considerations (e.g., beta‑blockers) and how they alter HR targets — in many cases RPE will be the better intensity guide.
  - Recommended monitoring (e.g., initial supervised sessions in cardiac rehab or medically supervised environment, use of ECG/HF monitoring for first sessions).

2) Preconditions before attempting HIIT
The client should meet all of the following:
- At least partly stable clinically for several months post‑MI (he’s 6 months out — good, but individual risk varies).
- No recent angina, uncontrolled arrhythmias, uncontrolled hypertension, decompensated heart failure, or other unstable cardiac/medical issues.
- Good baseline aerobic fitness and symptom‑free performance during the current moderate program (consistent multiple weeks of exercise without concerning symptoms, HR responses stable).
- Familiarity with interval training and excellent technique for any chosen modality (bike, treadmill, rower), and ability to adhere to strict breathing (no Valsalva).
- Preferably completed a supervised progression in cardiac rehab or similar supervised setting when first attempting higher intensities.

3) Recommended pathway to HIIT (progression and safeguards)
If cardiology clears, use a graded introduction — supervised, conservative, and monitored:

a. Supervised environment first
- First HIIT sessions performed under supervision (cardiac rehab, exercise physiologist, or trainer with AED and emergency plan) with continuous HR and symptom monitoring — ideally with ECG monitoring for initial sessions if clinician recommends.
- Start with low‑volume, conservative HIIT protocols.

b. Conservative HIIT templates to consider (examples)
- “Low‑volume/short‑interval” HIIT (safer starting point)
  - Warm‑up: 10–15 min easy
  - Work: 4 × 30–60 s high effort with 3–4 min active recovery (easy pedal/walk). Target peak intensity near but not exceeding agreed clinical HR (or RPE 15 if using RPE). Keep total high‑intensity time short (2–4 minutes).
  - Cool‑down: 10 min
- “Moderate low‑impact intervals”
  - Warm‑up 12–15 min
  - 6 × 1 min higher intensity with 2–3 min easy recovery
  - Total high intensity 6 minutes; monitor HR closely
- Progress only by increasing number of intervals or slightly lengthening work intervals; do not abruptly increase work intensity.

c. Intensity control
- Use clinician‑approved HR thresholds — do not exceed them. If on beta‑blockers, rely on RPE (aim RPE 14–15 for higher intensity intervals) rather than HR.
- Keep overall session RPE and symptom load acceptable; avoid pushing to exhaustion.
- Keep breathing coached: exhale on exertion, avoid Valsalva. Intervals should not involve heavy isometric efforts.

d. Frequency and progression
- Start with 1 HIIT session/week replacing one moderate session for 2–4 weeks, then reassess tolerance.
- If well tolerated (no ischemic symptoms, arrhythmias, excessive BP responses), consider increasing to up to 2 sessions/week but maintain majority of training as moderate intensity.
- Continue regular medical follow‑up and consider repeat stress testing if intending to sustain or progress HIIT long term.

4) Safer modality choices for HIIT
- Prefer modalities that are low impact and allow easy, immediate intensity changes: recumbent bike, upright cycle, elliptical, rower (if technique is solid).
- Treadmill hill sprints or running are higher risk because of impact and Valsalva tendency; use cautiously and only if cleared and supervised.

5) Monitoring and stop rules
- Continuous HR monitoring (chest strap more accurate) and subjective symptom checks (RPE, chest discomfort, dizziness, undue breathlessness, palpitations).
- Stop immediately and seek medical attention if chest pain/pressure, severe dyspnea, syncope, sustained palpitations, or pre‑syncope occur.
- Monitor BP pre/post sessions; abnormal rises (systolic >180 mmHg or diastolic >110 mmHg) warrant stopping and contacting clinician.

6) Example phased timeline (only after clearance)
- Phase A (2–4 weeks supervised): 1 session/week of very low volume HIIT (4 × 30–60 s efforts with long recoveries) + 2–3 moderate sessions/week.
- Phase B (4–6 weeks): If well tolerated, 1–2 sessions/week of 6 × 60–90 s intervals with 2–3 min recovery, still conservative. Continue strength training and longer moderate session(s).
- Maintenance: If cardiology approves and client tolerates, maintain 1–2 short HIIT sessions/week with ongoing monitoring. Emphasize overall weekly volume and recovery to support weight loss.

7) Alternatives to HIIT that increase caloric burn safely
If HIIT is not approved, you can still increase weight loss safely by:
- Increasing moderate‑intensity duration and frequency (longer steady sessions).
- Walking in hilly terrain or using incline intervals at moderate intensity (short hill bursts with careful HR monitoring).
- Increasing daily NEAT (steps) and resistance training volume/density as previously discussed.
- Incorporating longer low‑impact intervals at the high end of moderate intensity (e.g., 4–6 min bouts) which can be effective for caloric burn while safer than maximal intervals.

8) Documentation and shared decision making
- Get written clearance from cardiology specifying permitted intensity (%HRmax or VO2), recommended monitoring, and any absolute contraindications.
- Document the shared decision with the client, including risks discussed, emergency plan, and monitoring procedures.

Goal: increase total weekly aerobic volume while maintaining moderate intensity.

Weeks 5–8 (Build aerobic turnover and tempo work)

- Cardio frequency: 4–5 sessions/week.

  - Mon: Strength A + 20 min easy cardio
  - Tue: 40–45 min steady (include 20 min tempo at higher‑moderate effort)
  - Wed: Strength B + 15–20 min easy cardio
  - Thu: 30–35 min intervals: 6 × 3–4 min slightly higher pace with 2–3 min easy recovery (keep HR ≤115)
  - Fri: Strength C + 15 min easy cardio
  - Sat: 50–60 min longer walk/jog (progress jog time: 2 min jog/3 min walk → 3/2)
  - Sun: Rest or mobility

Weeks 9–10 (Specific 5K preparation)

  - Warm‑up 10–15 min easy

  - Cool‑down 10 min

  - Tue: 45 min steady with 25 min tempo (higher‑moderate)
  - Wed: Strength B + 15 min easy
  - Thu: 4–6 × 2–3 min faster segments with 2 min walking recovery (monitor HR)
  - Fri: Strength C + 15 min easy
  - Sat: 30–40 min brisk continuous run/walk rehearsal at anticipated race pace (or 3 km steady)
  - Sun: Rest

Weeks 11–12 (Taper, sharpen and test)

  - Thu: 4 × 1 min faster with 3 min easy recovery (short)
  - Fri: Rest or 20 min mobility
  - Sat: 20–30 min easy walk/jog
  - Sun: Rest

- Early week: 2 easy short sessions (20–30 min) with a few short pickups to stay sharp. Rest fully 48 hours before the time trial (or light activity day only).

  - Pre‑trial: rest, light meal 2–3 hours prior; hydrate; check resting vitals.
  - Warm‑up: 10–15 min easy walking/jog + dynamic drills, 2–3 short 30–60 s pickups at planned pace with full recovery.
  - Time trial: 5 km on a flat measured loop or treadmill. Aim to run/jog at the fastest sustainable pace that stays within cardiology‑approved HR limit. If cleared to exceed HR limit, follow the clinician’s prescribed ceiling.
  - During trial: monitor perceived exertion and any symptoms. You (trainer) should monitor HR and watch for signs of intolerance. Have an emergency plan and AED available.
  - Post‑trial: 10–15 min cool‑down walking and stretching; monitor vitals for at least 15–30 min.

Pacing and strategy notes
- If he cannot safely push HR high, use run/walk pacing to accumulate fast segments without long sustained HR elevation. For example, 1–2 min faster running with 1–2 min walking recovery repeated can produce a faster overall time while respecting HR limits.
- Use perceived exertion to guide surges: maintain effort that feels “hard but manageable” (RPE 13) for much of the trial if cleared for higher RPE; otherwise push to the upper allowed RPE.
- Teach breathing cues (exhale on exertion) and avoid breath‑holding. Encourage nasal breathing during easier parts if tolerable.

- Primary outcome: 5K time (minutes:seconds).
- Secondary outcomes: average HR during the 5K, peak HR, RPE, recovery HR after 1 and 5 minutes, and symptom log.
- Use the 5K time alongside other functional measures (30 s sit‑to‑stand, TUG, strength logs) to track overall fitness improvements.
- If the trial was performed without exceeding his safe HR ceiling, interpret improvements as meaningful even if not maximal.

Which compound lifts to add and why
- Back squat (progression through box/supported variations) — builds quadriceps, glutes, core and functional strength for sit‑to‑stand.
- Deadlift variations (Romanian deadlift, trap bar deadlift, hex bar) — emphasize posterior chain (hamstrings, glutes), grip, and functional hinge mechanics while limiting spinal shear.
- Alternatives/substitutes when needed: leg press, Bulgarian split squat, kettlebell goblet squat, Romanian deadlift with dumbbells, hip hinge on cable or rack pulls.

Goal: introduce squatting and hip‑hinge patterns with safe regressions, prioritize breathing and tempo.

  2. Romanian deadlift (RDL) with dumbbells — 3 × 10–12. Emphasize hip hinge, soft knee, long controlled eccentric (3–4 s), neutral spine. Rest 90–120 s.
  3. Assisted split squat or step‑downs — 2–3 × 8–12 each leg.
- Coaching cues:
  - Goblet squat: feet hip‑width, chest up, sit back to box, breathe: inhale down, exhale to stand; avoid holding breath.
  - RDL: push hips back, keep bar/Dbs close to legs, feel stretch in hamstrings, exhale on return to standing.
- HR/effort: Keep RPE 11–12. Use longer rests after RDLs if HR rises.

Weeks 3–4 (progress)
- Progress goblet squat load or lower box height; 3–4 sets × 8–12.
- Progress RDL weight slightly if HR and technique ok; add single‑leg RDL support variation 2–3 × 8–10 each leg for stability and unilateral strength.
- If balance and technique are solid, introduce trap/hex bar deadlift with very light load: 3 sets × 8–10 (long rests 120–180 s). Keep tempo controlled; coach breathing.

Phase 2 — Weeks 5–8: Progress to loaded compound variations (moderate loads)
Goal: allow progressive overload while maintaining cardiac safety.

- Trap bar deadlift (preferred progression) — 3–4 sets × 6–10. Use longer rests and controlled breathing. If no trap bar, perform barbell Romanian deadlift or rack pulls instead (lighter loads).

Phase 3 — Weeks 9–12: Consolidate compound strength (controlled heavier work)
Goal: further increase strength capacity with conservative heavier sets and maintain technique.

Weeks 9–10

  - The client demonstrates stable technique, good spinal control, no concerning HR or symptom responses during trap bar deadlifts and box squats.

- Maintain accessory unilateral work (split squats, step‑ups) 3 × 8–10.

- Duration: 12 weeks
- Weekly template (typical):
  - Mon: Strength A (Upper — heavier compound emphasis) + short cardio
  - Tue: Cardio steady or interval session (longer; walk/elliptical/bike)
  - Wed: Strength B (Lower — squats & deadlift progressions) + short cardio

- Cardio frequency: 4–5 sessions/week (mix of long steady, tempo, submax intervals below permitted HR or RPE).

- HR target: keep below clinician‑approved limit (≈115 bpm) during most training. If cardiology clears higher HR for time trial or HIIT, follow written guidance.
- RPE targets: Most sessions RPE 11–13 (light–moderate). Strength main compound sets may reach RPE 12–13 as tolerated. Only time trial or cleared HIIT may reach higher RPE under supervision.

Full 12‑week schedule (weeks grouped by phase). Each week lists the sessions with exercises, sets, reps, tempo and rest. Where progression is required, I note it.

PHASE 1 — Weeks 1–4: Foundation (technique, aerobic base, introduce compound patterns)
Goals: establish routine, teach breathing and movement, introduce goblet/box squats and RDLs, increase aerobic volume.

Weeks 1–2 (conservative start)
Weekly layout
- Mon — Strength A (Upper heavy emphasis) + 20–25 min easy cardio
- Tue — Cardio steady 25–30 min (brisk walk/elliptical/recumbent bike)
- Wed — Strength B (Lower technique & posterior chain) + 15–20 min easy cardio
- Thu — Active recovery: 20–30 min easy walk + mobility & breathing practice
- Fri — Strength C (Full‑body circuit) + 10–15 min easy cardio
- Sat — Long steady session: 35–45 min brisk walk or walk/jog intervals (start with 1 min jog / 4 min walk × 6–8)
- Sun — Rest or mobility

Session details

Strength A (Mon)
- Warm‑up: 8–10 min easy bike/walk + shoulder/upper mobility + breathing drill
- Main compound (machines preferred early):
  1. Seated chest press — 2 sets × 12–15 reps (tempo 2:3) — Rest 90 s
  2. Seated row (cable or machine) — 2 × 12–15 — Rest 90 s
  3. Seated overhead press (DB or machine) — 2 × 10–12 — Rest 90 s
- Accessory:
  4. Lat pulldown or assisted pull variation — 2 × 12–15 — Rest 60–75 s
  5. Incline machine flies or light DB flies — 2 × 12–15 — Rest 60–75 s
  6. Biceps curls — 2 × 12–15; Triceps pushdown — 2 × 12–15 — Superset optional (rest 60–75 s)
- Core/Grip: Farmer carry (light) 3 × 20–30 m; Dead bug 2 × 10–12
- Cool‑down: 8–10 min walk/cycle + stretches + diaphragmatic breathing (5 deep breaths)

Strength B (Wed) — Lower, technique focused
- Warm‑up: 8–10 min bike + dynamic hip mobility + bodyweight hip hinge drills
- Main:
  1. Goblet squat to box — 3 sets × 12–15 reps (2 s up / 3–4 s down) — Rest 90–120 s
  2. RDL with DBs — 3 × 10–12 (3–4 s eccentric) — Rest 120 s
  3. Assisted split squat or step‑downs — 2 × 10 each leg — Rest 90 s
- Accessory:
  4. Seated leg curl or stability ball hamstring curl — 2 × 12–15
  5. Standing calf raises (supported) — 3 × 12–15
- Balance/core: Single‑leg stand (assisted) 2 × 20–30 s each side; Pallof press 2 × 10 each side
- Cool‑down and breathing practice

Strength C (Fri) — Full‑body circuit (light)
- Warm‑up: 8 min easy cardio + mobility
- Circuit 2 rounds (progress to 3 rounds in Week 2) — 10–12 reps each, rest 60–90 s between exercises:
  1. Bodyweight or assisted goblet squat — 10–12
  2. TRX or machine row — 10–12
  3. DB RDL (light) — 10–12
  4. Machine chest press — 10–12
  5. Pallof press — 10 each side
  6. Farmer carry 30 s
- Cool‑down

Cardio sessions (Tue/Sat/Thu)
- Tue: 25–30 min steady (RPE 11–12)
- Thu: 20–30 min easy + mobility
- Sat: 35–45 min long walk or walk/jog (1:4 ratio) — keep HR <115

Progressions Weeks 3–4
- Increase sets on main lifts to 3–4 where tolerated.
- Progress goblet squat: reduce box height or increase DB load; 3–4 × 10–12.
- Introduce trap/hex bar deadlift (very light) 3 sets × 8–10 in Week 4 if technique and HR responses are good, rest 120–180 s.
- Increase cardio durations: Tue 35 min, Sat 45–55 min. Introduce one 4 × 1 min higher‑moderate pickups (keep HR monitored).

PHASE 2 — Weeks 5–8: Build (strength progression, unilateral work, increased cardio volume and tempo)
Goals: progressive overload, move toward trap bar deadlift & box safety squats, longer cardio, tempo sessions, balance work.

Weeks 5–6
Weekly layout (same as before but increase volume)
- Mon: Strength A + 20–30 min easy
- Tue: 40–45 min steady including 20 min tempo (higher‑moderate)
- Wed: Strength B + 20 min easy
- Thu: 30–35 min submax intervals: 6 × 4 min at upper‑moderate with 2–3 min easy recovery (keep HR ≤115)
- Fri: Strength C (circuit, denser) + 15–20 min easy
- Sat: 50–60 min long steady walk/jog (progressive jog time)
- Sun: Rest or active recovery

Strength A (Mon) — Increase load & sets
- Warm‑up
- Main compound: 4 sets × 8–10 for seated chest press, seated cable row, seated overhead press (rest 90–150 s)
- Add single‑arm row 3 × 8–10
- Accessory: 3 sets × 10–12 for flies, pulldown, biceps/triceps
- Core/grip: Farmer carries increasing distance; Pallof press 3 × 10 each side

Strength B (Wed) — Lower progression to trap bar & box squats
- Warm‑up: hip hinge drills and mobility
- Main:
  1. Box squat (safety bar or light barbell) — 3–4 × 8–10 (rest 120–180 s)
  2. Trap bar deadlift — 3–4 × 8–10 (rest 150–180 s)
  3. Bulgarian split squat (assisted) — 3 × 8–10 each leg — Rest 90–120 s
- Accessory:
  4. Glute bridge or hip thrust — 3 × 10–12
  5. Seated leg curl — 3 × 12–15
- Core/balance: single‑leg RDL support 2 × 8 each leg; plank 2 × 20–30 s

Strength C (Fri) — Denser full‑body circuit
- Warm‑up
- Circuit: 3–4 rounds of:
  1. Goblet squat 10–12
  2. TRX row or cable row 10–12
  3. Trap bar deadlift (lighter) 8–10
  4. DB incline press 10–12
  5. Farmer carry 40 m
  6. Core: dead bug or Pallof 10 each side
- Keep between‑exercise rest 60–90 s; longer rest between rounds 2–3 min.

Cardio (Tue/Thu/Sat)
- Tue: 40–45 min with 20 min tempo (RPE 12–13)
- Thu: 6 × 4 min higher‑moderate with 2–3 min recovery; aim HR near upper‑moderate but ≤115
- Sat: 50–60 min long steady; progress walk/jog to 3 min jog / 2 min walk as tolerated

Weeks 7–8 — continue progressions
- Increase sets on main lifts to 4 where tolerated: box squat 4 × 6–8 (slightly lower reps/higher load if RPE allows), trap bar deadlift 4 × 6–8.
- Emphasize eccentric control (3–4 s) and time under tension to drive strength without raising HR too much.
- Cardio: one session longer (60 min), tempo sessions 25–30 min, intervals maintained but ensure HR safe.

PHASE 3 — Weeks 9–12: Consolidate, specificity for 5K, strength consolidation (controlled heavier work)
Goals: maintain strength increases (barbell back squat and heavier trap bar deadlift if cleared), sharpen run fitness for 5K, taper before time trial.

Weeks 9–10 — Specific build for 5K
Weekly layout shifts slightly to include run rehearsals
- Mon: Strength A (Upper, slightly lighter if run rehearsal later) + 20 min easy
- Tue: Running-specific session: 30–40 min including 15–20 min at tempo/goal pace (or controlled run/walk intervals)
- Wed: Strength B (Lower: barbell progression and posterior chain) + 15–20 min easy
- Thu: Interval session on bike/elliptical or treadmill: 4–6 × 2–3 min faster with 2 min recovery (monitor HR)
- Fri: Strength C (Full‑body circuit) + 10–15 min easy
- Sat: Long steady run/walk 40–60 min (aim to increase continuous running time gradually)
- Sun: Rest or active recovery

Strength A (Mon)
- Maintain 3–4 sets × 6–10 on upper compounds (chest press, rows, overhead press) — RPE ≤13 — rest 90–150 s
- Accessory work 3 × 10–12 and core work

Strength B (Wed) — heavier compound emphasis
- Progressions only if cleared and technique is solid:
  1. Back squat (shallow free barbell or safety bar) — only if technique and HR control ok — start very light: 3–4 × 6–8 — rest 120–180 s.
  2. Trap bar deadlift or RDL — 4 × 6–8 — rest 150–180 s.
  3. Bulgarian split squat 3 × 8 each leg
- Accessory: hip thrusts, hamstring curls, calf raises, single‑leg RDLs.

Strength C (Fri)
- Full body circuit with heavier emphasis on functional strength but keep density moderate so HR does not exceed limit:
  - 3 rounds of: Goblet squat 8–10, TRX row 8–10, DB RDL 8–10, DB bench 8–10, carry 40 m, Pallof press 10 each side. Rest 90–120 s between rounds.

Cardio / Run specifics
- Tuesday tempo: 15–20 min at higher‑moderate effort in a 30–40 min session (keep HR monitored).
- Thursday intervals: use short, controlled intervals but keep HR ≤115.
- Saturday longer run: aim to increase continuous running/walking time up to a 30–40 min continuous jog/walk (as tolerated). Progress run segments week‑to‑week.

Weeks 11–12 — Taper and test (5K)
Week 11 — taper & sharpen
- Reduce overall volume by ~15–20% from Week 10. Maintain some intensity but shorter efforts.
- Strength: reduce volume and intensity (lightened loads, shorter sessions), keep technique.
- Cardio: 2 short tempo/rehearsal sessions (midweek); reduce Saturday long run to 30–40 min easy.
- Focus on recovery, sleep & nutrition.

Week 12 — race week (5K time trial)
- Early week (Mon–Wed): 2 easy short sessions (20–30 min) with a few short pickups (30–60 s) to stay sharp.
- Avoid heavy squats/deadlifts in the 7 days prior to time trial; do light technique work only.
- Rest 48 hours before the trial (or do short easy activity day).
- Time trial day (trainer present; AED & emergency plan ready):
  - Pre‑trial: light meal 2–3 hours before; check vitals; confirm no symptoms.
  - Warm‑up: 10–15 min easy walk/jog + dynamic drills + 2–3 short pickups at planned pace.
  - 5K time trial: on flat measured loop or treadmill. Pace according to clinician limits: if cardiology allows HR to exceed 115 for the test, follow the prescribed ceiling; otherwise, perform a maximal effort within HR cap (use RPE if on beta‑blockers).
  - Cool‑down: 10–15 min walking & stretching; monitor HR and symptoms for 15–30 min after.
- Post‑trial: record 5K time, average/peak HR, RPE, and note recovery HR at 1 and 5 minutes. Contact cardiologist if abnormal symptoms.

Sample daily sessions (one after the other) — concrete examples

Example Week 6 (mid‑program) — fully written day sessions
- Monday: Strength A + 20 min easy bike
  - Warm‑up 10 min easy cycle
  - Seated chest press 4 × 8–10 (90–150 s rest)
  - Seated cable row 4 × 8–10
  - Seated overhead press 3 × 8–10
  - Single‑arm DB row 3 × 8–10 each
  - Biceps curls 3 × 12 superset triceps pushdown 3 × 12
  - Farmer carry 3 × 30 m
  - Cool‑down 15 min easy bike + stretching
- Tuesday: Cardio (Tempo) 40–45 min
  - Warm‑up 8–10 min
  - 20 min tempo (higher‑moderate) — keep HR under limit
  - Cool‑down 8–10 min + mobility & breathing
- Wednesday: Strength B (Lower heavy) + 15 min walk
  - Warm‑up 8–10 min
  - Box squat (safety bar) 4 × 8 (120–180 s rest)
  - Trap bar deadlift 4 × 8 (150–180 s rest)
  - Bulgarian split squat 3 × 8 each
  - Glute bridge 3 × 10–12
  - Single‑leg RDL 2 × 8 each
  - Cool‑down walk 15 min + stretching
- Thursday: Intervals 6 × 4 min on bike with 2 min easy recoveries (HR monitored)
- Friday: Strength C Circuit (3 rounds) + 15 min easy
- Saturday: Long steady 55–60 min walk/jog
- Sunday: Rest

Progression rules (quick recap)
- Increase sets (from 2 → 3 → 4) in early weeks then increase load conservatively.
- Only increase weight when last set RPE ≤12 and HR recovery acceptable.
- Increase cardio volume by no more than ~10–15% per week.
- If HR approaches limit repeatedly, reduce load or duration and reassess with clinician.

Compound lifts specifics and coaching cues (safety)
- Goblet squat → Box squat → Safety bar or shallow barbell back squat progression; never force deep free back squats until technique and HR tolerance proven.
- RDL → Trap bar deadlift → heavier trap bar or cautious barbell deadlift only if clearance and technique permit.
- Breathing: inhale on lowering, exhale on stand/drive; avoid breath‑holding. Cue exhale on concentric.
- Rest 120–180 s after heavy sets; monitor HR recovery.

- No true HIIT unless cardiologist clears. If cleared later, introduce very conservative low‑volume HIIT (e.g., 4 × 30–60 s with long recovery) under supervision, then progress cautiously.
- For weight loss without HIIT, maintain increased moderate cardio volume and resistance training.

Monitoring, outcome measures and record keeping
- Track: session RPE, peak HR during sessions and recovery HR at 1 and 5 minutes, BP pre and post (if possible), weights lifted / reps, and symptoms.
- Functional tests at baseline and Week 12: 30 s sit‑to‑stand, timed up & go (TUG), single leg balance, farmer carry distance/weight, and the 5K time.
- Use weekly weigh‑ins (same day/time), waist circumference, and training logs to evaluate progress.
- Reassess medically and adjust plan if abnormal responses occur.

Nutrition support (summary)
- Maintain Mediterranean pattern, modest caloric deficit ~300–500 kcal/day, protein 1.0–1.2 g/kg/day, low sodium, 2 servings oily fish/week, fiber ≥25–30 g/day.
- Pre/post workout snacks as required (small carb + protein).
- If you want, provide a 7‑day menu tuned to his exact calorie target (give me bodyweight and whether he wants to lose ~0.25 or 0.5 kg/week).

Safety checklist for each session (trainer)
- Pre‑session: confirm no chest pain, dizziness, syncope, severe breathlessness. Check resting HR & BP if indicated.
- Equipment: HR monitor working, phone and AED visible, emergency action plan known.
- During session: continuous observation, HR check frequently, cue breathing and avoid Valsalva.
- Post‑session: cool down 8–15 min, check vitals, ask about symptoms, record data.

Below is a complete 12‑week, clinic‑grade programme you can give your 58‑year‑old male client who is six months post‑MI, cardiac‑rehab cleared for moderate intensity (target HR ≲ ~115 bpm / ≈70% age‑predicted max), no Valsalva, and no maximal lifts. It integrates all prior adjustments: increased strength (including squats/deadlifts progressions), higher safe cardio volume to support weight loss, cardiac‑safe interval work, nutrition guidance, and a 5K time‑trial target at the end of Week 12. Safety and monitoring guidance is repeated where essential.

Important preface (read and act on these before starting)
- Obtain and document medical clearance for the plan; if any part (e.g., 5K maximal effort, HIIT, or heavier compound lifts) requires higher intensity than the current clearance, get explicit written cardiologist approval.
- If client is on beta‑blockers (or other HR‑blunting meds), use RPE as primary intensity gauge (target RPE zones indicated). If not on HR‑blunting meds, use HR + RPE.
- Trainer must monitor symptoms continuously; stop exercise and follow emergency procedures for chest pain, syncope, severe dizziness, sustained palpitations, or concerning arrhythmia.
- Use continuous HR monitoring (chest strap preferred) in sessions. Keep breaths steady and exhale on exertion; strictly avoid breath‑holding/Valsalva.
- No 1RM/max testing. Progress by small increments (2–5%) and by adding sets/reps and improving technique and time under tension.

Program summary
- Duration: 12 weeks
- Weekly template (typical):
  - Mon: Strength A (Upper — heavier compound emphasis) + short cardio
  - Tue: Cardio steady or interval session (longer; walk/elliptical/bike)
  - Wed: Strength B (Lower — squats & deadlift progressions) + short cardio
  - Thu: Active recovery / mobility + optional moderate cardio or interval session
  - Fri: Strength C (Full‑body circuit, higher density) + short cardio
  - Sat: Long steady cardio (walk/run/walk‑jog progressive) or outdoor activity
  - Sun: Rest or active recovery (stretching, gentle walk)
- Strength frequency: 3 sessions/week (structured heavy compound days Mon/Wed and a circuit Fri).
- Cardio frequency: 4–5 sessions/week (mix of long steady, tempo, submax intervals below permitted HR or RPE).
- 5K time trial scheduled for the end of Week 12 (only with documented medical clearance to attempt the trial; perform supervised).

Intensity guidelines
- HR target: keep below clinician‑approved limit (≈115 bpm) during most training. If cardiology clears higher HR for time trial or HIIT, follow written guidance.
- RPE targets: Most sessions RPE 11–13 (light–moderate). Strength main compound sets may reach RPE 12–13 as tolerated. Only time trial or cleared HIIT may reach higher RPE under supervision.
- Rest: 90–180 s for main compound sets; 60–90 s for accessory/circuit exercises.

Nutrition summary (as previously provided)
- Mediterranean‑style, plant‑forward.
- Calorie plan: modest deficit ~300–500 kcal/day from maintenance to promote ~0.25–0.5 kg/week weight loss (adjust to his bodyweight; we can make specific daily targets with his weight).
- Protein: ~1.0–1.2 g/kg/day, distributed across meals (20–30 g per meal).
- Sodium: ≤2,300 mg/day (or per clinician).
- Pre/post workout carbs + protein: small snack before (banana + peanut butter) and post (Greek yogurt + fruit).
- Hydration, sleep (7–9 h), stress management, and follow‑up labs per cardiologist.

How to use the plan
- Follow the weekly session schedule. Track session RPE, HR peaks, BP before/after sessions (if possible), sets/reps/weights, symptoms.
- Increase loads only if last set RPE ≤12 and HR recovery is acceptable. Increase 2–5% at a time.
- Taper strength volume in Week 12 before the 5K (reduce intensity/volume by ~30–40% in the 7 days prior).

Full 12‑week schedule (weeks grouped by phase). Each week lists the sessions with exercises, sets, reps, tempo and rest. Where progression is required, I note it.

PHASE 1 — Weeks 1–4: Foundation (technique, aerobic base, introduce compound patterns)
Goals: establish routine, teach breathing and movement, introduce goblet/box squats and RDLs, increase aerobic volume.

Weeks 1–2 (conservative start)
Weekly layout
- Mon — Strength A (Upper heavy emphasis) + 20–25 min easy cardio
- Tue — Cardio steady 25–30 min (brisk walk/elliptical/recumbent bike)
- Wed — Strength B (Lower technique & posterior chain) + 15–20 min easy cardio
- Thu — Active recovery: 20–30 min easy walk + mobility & breathing practice
- Fri — Strength C (Full‑body circuit) + 10–15 min easy cardio
- Sat — Long steady session: 35–45 min brisk walk or walk/jog intervals (start with 1 min jog / 4 min walk × 6–8)
- Sun — Rest or mobility

Session details

Strength A (Mon)
- Warm‑up: 8–10 min easy bike/walk + shoulder/upper mobility + breathing drill
- Main compound (machines preferred early):
  1. Seated chest press — 2 sets × 12–15 reps (tempo 2:3) — Rest 90 s
  2. Seated row (cable or machine) — 2 × 12–15 — Rest 90 s
  3. Seated overhead press (DB or machine) — 2 × 10–12 — Rest 90 s
- Accessory:
  4. Lat pulldown or assisted pull variation — 2 × 12–15 — Rest 60–75 s
  5. Incline machine flies or light DB flies — 2 × 12–15 — Rest 60–75 s
  6. Biceps curls — 2 × 12–15; Triceps pushdown — 2 × 12–15 — Superset optional (rest 60–75 s)
- Core/Grip: Farmer carry (light) 3 × 20–30 m; Dead bug 2 × 10–12
- Cool‑down: 8–10 min walk/cycle + stretches + diaphragmatic breathing (5 deep breaths)

Strength B (Wed) — Lower, technique focused
- Warm‑up: 8–10 min bike + dynamic hip mobility + bodyweight hip hinge drills
- Main:
  1. Goblet squat to box — 3 sets × 12–15 reps (2 s up / 3–4 s down) — Rest 90–120 s
  2. RDL with DBs — 3 × 10–12 (3–4 s eccentric) — Rest 120 s
  3. Assisted split squat or step‑downs — 2 × 10 each leg — Rest 90 s
- Accessory:
  4. Seated leg curl or stability ball hamstring curl — 2 × 12–15
  5. Standing calf raises (supported) — 3 × 12–15
- Balance/core: Single‑leg stand (assisted) 2 × 20–30 s each side; Pallof press 2 × 10 each side
- Cool‑down and breathing practice

Strength C (Fri) — Full‑body circuit (light)
- Warm‑up: 8 min easy cardio + mobility
- Circuit 2 rounds (progress to 3 rounds in Week 2) — 10–12 reps each, rest 60–90 s between exercises:
  1. Bodyweight or assisted goblet squat — 10–12
  2. TRX or machine row — 10–12
  3. DB RDL (light) — 10–12
  4. Machine chest press — 10–12
  5. Pallof press — 10 each side
  6. Farmer carry 30 s

Progression rules (quick recap)
- Increase sets (from 2 → 3 → 4) in early weeks then increase load conservatively.
- Only increase weight when last set RPE ≤12 and HR recovery acceptable.
- Increase cardio volume by no more than ~10–15% per week.
- If HR approaches limit repeatedly, reduce load or duration and reassess with clinician.

Compound lifts specifics and coaching cues (safety)
- Goblet squat → Box squat → Safety bar or shallow barbell back squat progression; never force deep free back squats until technique and HR tolerance proven.
- RDL → Trap bar deadlift → heavier trap bar or cautious barbell deadlift only if clearance and technique permit.
- Breathing: inhale on lowering, exhale on stand/drive; avoid breath‑holding. Cue exhale on concentric.
- Rest 120–180 s after heavy sets; monitor HR recovery.

Safe HIIT & higher intensity note
- No true HIIT unless cardiologist clears. If cleared later, introduce very conservative low‑volume HIIT (e.g., 4 × 30–60 s with long recovery) under supervision, then progress cautiously.
- For weight loss without HIIT, maintain increased moderate cardio volume and resistance training.
